questions.q: How does Prometheus typically get metrics from an application, compared to Azure Monitor or CloudWatch?
options: It pulls them by scraping an HTTP endpoint on a schedule, rather than the app pushing them
It reads them directly from the application's source code
It requires the application to write metrics to a shared database file
It has no way to collect metrics from applications, only infrastructure
questions.explain: Prometheus uses a pull model: the server scrapes a /metrics HTTP endpoint on each target on a schedule, instead of applications pushing data out like they do with Azure Monitor or CloudWatch.

questions.q: What is the TSDB in Prometheus's architecture?
options: A third-party database you must install separately
Prometheus's built-in time-series database, indexing data by metric name and labels
The dashboard UI for viewing graphs
A tool for sending alerts to Slack
questions.explain: TSDB is Prometheus's own purpose-built storage engine, built into the server, indexing every time series by its metric name and label set.

questions.q: Why does Prometheus need service discovery on Kubernetes?
options: Kubernetes doesn't support HTTP scraping
Pods are created and destroyed dynamically, so a static list of IPs to scrape wouldn't stay accurate
Service discovery replaces the need for the TSDB
It's only needed for alerting, not metrics collection
questions.explain: On Kubernetes, pods are rescheduled and IPs change constantly, especially during autoscaling. Service discovery lets Prometheus continuously ask the Kubernetes API what to scrape instead of relying on a static list.

options: It's the primary way all applications should send metrics to Prometheus
It replaces Alertmanager for routing alerts
It lets short-lived batch jobs push final metric values for Prometheus to scrape later, since they'd exit before a normal scrape would catch them
It stores long-term historical data instead of the TSDB
questions.explain: The Pushgateway is a deliberate exception to the pull model, meant specifically for short-lived jobs. Long-running services like Northbridge's checkout service should always be scraped directly.

questions.q: What role does Alertmanager play in Prometheus's architecture?
options: It scrapes metrics from applications instead of the Prometheus server
It's a separate process that receives firing alerts from the server and handles grouping, deduplication, silencing, and routing
It stores the raw time-series data
It replaces PromQL for writing queries
questions.explain: The Prometheus server evaluates alerting rules and pushes firing alerts to Alertmanager, a separate process dedicated to grouping, deduplicating, silencing, and routing those alerts to destinations like email or Slack.
